To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) morphine withdrawal induces the activation of noradrenergetic neurons in the NTS‐A1/A2 and VLM‐A1 cell groups and in their projection area in the PVN; (2) morphine withdrawal increases TH levels and TH enzyme activation in the NTS/A2/VLM‐cell groups and in the target area of these neurons in the PVN.
morphine dependence induces adaptive changes in noradrenergics neurons innervating the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVN).

morphine withdrawal increases the activity and protein expression of the rate‐limitin enzyme in catecholsynthesis, the tyrosine hydroxyylase (TH) in noradrenerg neurons in the NTS‐A/VLM‐A cell groups that innervate the PVN and in the PVH itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of catecholaminergics in the brainstem during morphine withdrawal, and its relationship to HPA activation.
the regulation of catecholamine levels and activity during morphine withdrawal and the role of these catecholamine systems in mediating opioid withdrawal symptoms.
the mechanisms that underlie the enhanced HPA axis activity in the rat following morphine withdrawal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increase in TH levels in NTS‐A1/A2 neurons during morphine abstinence might represent an adaptive change to the increased noradrenergically mediated HPA axis activity, and might be involved in the development of morphine abstinence syndrome.
morphine withdrawal is associated with an activation of catecholaminergics systems, which might contribute to the HPA activation during morphine withdrawal.
during morphine withdrawal there is a significant increase in TH protein expression, enzyme activity and neuronal activation in noradrenergically‐innervated brain areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the morphine withdrawal‐induced increase in noradrenergics activity is mediated through an adaptive change of noradrenergic neurons, including an increase in TH levels and activity, in the NTS‐A/VLM‐A noradrenergies cell groups, which innervate the PVN.
morphine withdrawal increases noradrenergically mediated HPA activity by an increase in the activity of the noradrenergics systems innervating the HPA.
morphine withdrawal induces an activation of catecholaminergics neurons of the NTS/VLm, which is associated with an increase of TH protein levels in the NTS‐A1/A2 neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

opioid dependence is accompanied by a hyperactivity of the NTS‐A1/VLM‐A2 catecholaminergics neurons, which innervate the PVN, and that this hyperactivity might be involved in the activation of the HPA axis during morphine withdrawal.

opioid withdrawal is associated with changes in the activity of the HPA axis, which is mediated, at least in part, by an increase in the activity of noradrenergetic pathways innervating hypothalamic PVNs.
morphine withdrawal induces an increased expression of TH and an increase in TH activity in the PVNs.
